levels.name: Joker Strategy 2314
levels.tagline: Use Jokers to accelerate, adapt, and win.
levels.outcomes:
By the end of this course, players will be able to understand the correct use of jokers in American Mahjong, identify when a joker is legal or not legal, and complete joker exchanges in the correct order.

Players will also learn how to avoid common joker mistakes, protect their hand from becoming dead, and make smarter decisions when using or exchanging jokers. This course helps players build confidence, improve accuracy, and use jokers as a strategic advantage during the game.
levels.description:
Jokers are one of the most powerful tiles in American Mahjong, but they are also one of the most commonly misunderstood. Used correctly, they can strengthen your hand, open up new possibilities, and help you move closer to Mahjong. Used incorrectly, they can cost you the game or even make your hand dead.

The Joker Strategy Course teaches players how to use jokers with confidence, clarity, and strategy. Through practical examples and real table situations, players will learn the correct rules for joker use, joker exchange, exposed jokers, and the mistakes to avoid during play.

levels.description: This level focuses on developing hands with greater complexity and higher value. You will learn the principles of flexible hand building — how to keep your options open while progressing toward a strong winning hand, and how to maximise your tiles' potential at every stage of the game.
keyTakeaways: Building towards high-value winning hands
Managing tile flexibility and avoiding over-commitment
Understanding hand efficiency and speed
Recognising and using bonus tiles effectively
Developing backup hands and knowing when to switch
Balancing hand strength with defensive safety

levels.name: Tactical Play
levels.tagline: Make smarter moves by understanding the whole table.
levels.outcomes: By the end of this level, you will be playing with full awareness of the table — using information from all four players to make sharper, more informed decisions every round.
levels.description: Tactical play is about using information from the entire table to your advantage. This level teaches you how to track discards, read the state of the game, understand what your opponents are likely building, and respond tactically — whether by accelerating, defending, or disrupting.
keyTakeaways: Reading the discard pile to assess opponent strategies
Understanding when opponents are close to winning
Tactical discarding: giving away less while building more
Responding to claimed tiles and declared sets
Managing table position and relative score
Timing attacks and defences based on game state

levels.name: Scoring & Analysis
levels.tagline: Master the scoring system and make every hand count.
levels.outcomes: After this level, scoring will no longer be a mystery — you will use it as an active tool to guide your hand selection, raise your average score, and play with greater strategic purpose.
levels.description: Understanding the scoring system deeply changes how you play. This level teaches you how Western Mahjong scoring works in full — from base points to bonuses and penalties — and how to use that knowledge to target higher-value hands, calculate risk accurately, and make better decisions in pivotal moments.
keyTakeaways: The complete Western Mahjong scoring system
High-value hand categories and how to target them
Self-draw bonuses and how to pursue them
Scoring penalties and how to avoid them
Using score awareness to guide in-game decisions
Post-game self-analysis and improvement habits

levels.name: Advanced Mastery
levels.tagline: Complete mastery — confident, strategic, and consistent.
levels.outcomes: You will complete your Western Mahjong journey with the confidence, knowledge, and strategic depth to play at a high level in any setting — and to keep improving beyond this programme.
levels.description: The final level of the Western Mahjong journey integrates every skill developed across the previous five levels into polished, full-game play. You will practise complete games at a competitive standard, refine your decision-making in complex situations, and build the consistency and composure that define mastery.
keyTakeaways: Full competitive game simulation and debrief
Advanced defensive techniques and table control
Managing momentum, comebacks, and pressure
Complex hand strategies and situational decision-making
Building consistency across multiple games
Applying all six levels in complete, high-level play

content.title: Mahjong Success Circle
content.subtitle: Mahjong is a game built for four. Our Circles bring players together beyond the classroom — for regular games, shared rituals, and lasting friendships.

content.desc1: A Circle is a small, regular group of Mahjong players who meet to play, learn, and connect. Unlike a casual game night, a Circle has continuity — the same people, the same table, building something together over time.
content.desc2: Each Circle is formed from players at a similar level, so the game stays balanced and the conversation stays meaningful. Whether you join an existing Circle or help form a new one, you're stepping into a ready-made community.
content.desc3: Circles meet regularly — fortnightly or monthly — in a relaxed, social setting. There's no pressure to perform. The goal is simple: show up, play well, and enjoy the company.
content.title: What is a Circle?

features.desc: Every Circle is built around a core group of four — the perfect number for a full, balanced table.
features.title: 4 Players

features.desc: Circles meet on a consistent schedule, giving you a rhythm and something to look forward to each week.
features.title: Regular Sessions

features.desc: Players are grouped by experience so the game stays engaging and the learning stays relevant.

features.desc: Circles aren't one-off events. They're ongoing — designed to grow into friendships that extend beyond the table.
features.title: Built to Last

content.title: Benefits of Joining a Circle

benefits.desc: Nothing improves your game faster than regular play. Circle members develop intuition, speed, and strategy that classroom sessions alone can't replicate.
benefits.title: Accelerated Progress

benefits.desc: You'll start to read players, spot patterns, and discuss decisions after hands. The table becomes a place of genuine strategic exchange.
benefits.title: Real Table Conversation

benefits.desc: You know who you're playing with. That consistency creates comfort, trust, and eventually — friendship.
benefits.title: Consistent Company

benefits.desc: In a busy life, a regular Circle gives you something to anchor to — a dedicated time, a familiar place, and people who are genuinely glad you're there.
benefits.title: A Ritual to Return To

benefits.desc: Mahjong has always been a social act. Joining a Circle means becoming part of something with history, inside jokes, and a shared language.
benefits.title: Belonging

benefits.desc: Regular play deepens your appreciation of the game's heritage — the etiquette, the rhythms, and the rituals that make Mahjong unlike any other game.
benefits.title: Cultural Connection

content.subtitle: The classroom teaches you how to play. The Circle is where you truly learn — through repetition, conversation, and the particular magic of a game played with people you know.

howItWorks.desc: Circles are open to students who have completed at least Level 1 (Foundation). You need to know the tiles, the rules, and the basics of hand-building — the Circle takes it from there.
howItWorks.label: Who Can Join

howItWorks.desc: Each session runs for approximately 2 to 3 hours. You'll play multiple rounds, discuss strategy between hands, and close with a brief recap of the key moments.
howItWorks.label: Session Format

howItWorks.desc: Most Circles meet fortnightly or monthly, on a day and time agreed by the group. You can join an existing Circle with a matching schedule or help form a new one.
howItWorks.label: Meeting Frequency

howItWorks.desc: Sessions are hosted at coffee shops in an informal setting — tiles provided, tea on the table, relaxed comfortable environment.
howItWorks.label: Location

howItWorks.desc: A full Circle is four players. We sometimes run sessions with a rotating fifth member to allow flexibility and keep the group active when someone can't make it.
howItWorks.label: Group Size

howItWorks.desc: There's no lock-in. Circles work best when members attend consistently, but life happens — just let the group know in advance and we'll manage around you.
howItWorks.label: Commitment
